cards.title: Introduction to Asynchronous Programming
cards.content:
Asynchronous programming is a concurrent programming model that allows your program to perform other tasks while waiting for operations—like network requests or file I/O—to finish.

In Python, this is primarily achieved using the asyncio library, async/await syntax, and event loops.

content.question: What is the primary benefit of asynchronous programming over synchronous programming in I/O bound tasks?

options.text: It executes CPU-heavy math operations faster.
It prevents the main thread from blocking while waiting for I/O operations.
It automatically uses all available CPU cores.
It requires less memory than synchronous code.

cards.title: Async and Await Syntax
cards.content:
To define a coroutine function in Python, you use the async def syntax.

import asyncio

async def main():
    print("Hello")
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    print("World")

asyncio.run(main())

The await keyword pauses the execution of the coroutine until the awaited result is ready, allowing other tasks to run in the meantime.

cards.title: Running Tasks Concurrently
cards.content:
To run multiple coroutines concurrently, asyncio.gather() is commonly used.

import asyncio

async def fetch_data(id, delay):
    print(f"Task {id}: starting")
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
    print(f"Task {id}: done")
    return f"data {id}"

async def main():
    results = await asyncio.gather(
        fetch_data(1, 2),
        fetch_data(2, 1)
    )
    print(results)

asyncio.run(main())

pairs.right: Pauses coroutine execution until result is ready
Entry point that manages the event loop

steps: Define a coroutine using async def
Await an asynchronous operation inside the coroutine
Pass the coroutine to asyncio.run() to execute the event loop

cards.title: Common Pitfalls in Async Python
cards.content:
Be careful not to block the event loop! Using synchronous blocking libraries (like time.sleep() or standard requests) inside an async function will freeze the entire event loop.

Always use asynchronous alternatives like asyncio.sleep() or httpx/aiohttp for network requests.
